Release note drafted and the mechanism is in place.

PR #950 is labelled 'type: breaking', so the change lands under Breaking in the drafted release. Release Drafter only emits PR titles, so the consumer-facing paragraph was posted as a comment on #950 for whoever cuts the release to paste into the draft: morphir-runtime_3 stops being produced, consumers move to morphir-runtime-classic_3, the Scala package is unchanged so it is a build-file change only, and morphir-naming_3 / morphir-model_3 appear as new artifacts with morphir depending transitively on naming.

Flagged on the PR as well: 'type: breaking' maps to a major bump in version-resolver, which on a 0.x line resolves to 1.0.0 and is very likely not intended. The tag should be set deliberately at release time.

The detail also remains in morphir/model/CONTRIBUTING.md item 7, which is the checked-in copy.

The 'consider configuring MiMa' half of this issue is split into morphir-1pr rather than dropped — and note MiMa would not actually have caught this, since it compares an artifact against its own previous version and says nothing when one disappears.

Resolved in fc575135 by dropping the trait rather than by publishing the modules.

All seven trees — langkit/core, langkit/trees, langkit/elm/core, langkit/elm/compiler/api, kit/kyo, intelligence, intelligence/sdk — no longer extend MorphirPublishModule / MorphirIntelligencePublishModule. Publishing them would have committed those coordinates and their API surface permanently, since a Maven Central release cannot be withdrawn, and none is ready for that. Nothing in the published set depends on them, so nothing downstream changes.

./mill resolve 'morphir.__.publishSonatypeCentral' now yields exactly the modules the publish command names plus the mill-morphir-elm plugin it deliberately excludes, so the discrepancy is gone by construction. The publish task records that invariant, the resolve command to check it, and the rule that a module which should not ship drops the trait instead of being omitted from the list.

Answers to the two questions this issue posed: intelligence and intelligence/sdk used MorphirIntelligencePublishModule, which is just MorphirPublishModule with a different pom organization, so no separate publish path existed for them. And the drift concern is addressed by making the trait the single declaration of intent, rather than by a CI guard.

Two reversible costs, recorded in the commit message: these modules lose publishLocal, and they fall out of the  smoke test in test:jvm/test:js. Re-adding the trait restores both when any of them is ready to be released.

Obsolete, not done. This called for splitting the markdown langkit into a -core module beneath a container directory. That split is unnecessary: a Mill directory can be a published module AND the parent of nested modules at once. morphir/model publishes as morphir-model while morphir/model/lowering publishes as morphir-model-lowering (both verified with ./mill show). So morphir-langkit-markdown keeps its coordinate, its package, and every consumer, and the two writers are simply added beneath it as morphir-langkit-markdown-compiler-scalatags and morphir-langkit-markdown-compiler-kyo-ui. No rename, no churn in morphir-knowledge-okf or build.mill. Intent 0033, intent 0021, intent 0022 and the published-library-families Design Note all updated to drop -core.

JVM+JS only: the Native variant fails at nativeLink because kyo-ui transitively pulls kyo-net/kyo-http whose C sources need BoringSSL/OpenSSL symbols; tracked as morphir-je9.8, and intent 0033 updated to state the split.

Done (commit 67ebafb2). KnowledgeBrowserView.conceptView parses the concept body and compiles it through KyoUiCompiler instead of folding raw Markdown into a paragraph. An unparseable body renders a diagnostic rather than raising, so one malformed concept cannot blank the browser. Settles intent 0033's Wasm open question: the answer is yes - conceptView is in sources shared by morphir/ui's js and wasm modules, so the writer links for both, which gave morphir-langkit-markdown and langkit-core wasm variants (none a publish module). morphir/ui passes on js and wasm; desktop still compiles.

Solved (commit 823d6f93). Native support restored: 10/10 tests pass on JVM, JS and Native, full native suite green at 277.

ROOT CAUSE: not missing libraries, but missing link flags. kyo-net compiles its TLS shim (kyo_tls.c, kyo_net_openssl.c, kyo_net_boringssl.c) into the binary and deliberately emits no Scala Native @link, because no kyonet_openssl shared library exists to name. kyo's own OpenSslBindings.scala says so: 'the system OpenSSL is linked via the openssl-native-settings link options (-lssl -lcrypto)'. Supplying them is the consuming build's job.

FIX: MorphirNativeOpenSsl in build.mill adds -lssl -lcrypto. No -L needed - Scala Native already searches /opt/homebrew/lib on macOS and /usr/lib on Linux; my first attempt added a Homebrew keg path that turned out redundant.

KEY GOTCHA: the trait must be mixed into the nested test module too. A nested 'object test' does NOT inherit nativeLinkingOptions, so the first experiment still failed to link even though 'mill show <module>.nativeLinkingOptions' proved the flags were present - the test module showed only -L/opt/homebrew/lib. Documented on the trait.

CI: install-libuv.sh renamed to install-native-deps.sh and now installs libssl-dev alongside libuv1-dev; the C shim needs headers at compile time and shared objects at link time.
